packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

packet-06 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. I listed the packet directory (filenames only, which showed packet.json exists); I did not open packet.json. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules except that listing.

LAYOUT SURVEY

image-001.jpg (overview, face 1): Book photographed open, upright. Left page: a parchment leaf (last leaf of the text block, verso, apparently) with heavily abbreviated text in two columns, brown ink, small cursive (Anglicana-type) hand with extreme abbreviation (superscript letters, suspension marks throughout). Heavy brown staining across the whole leaf, worst in the left column centre and along the bottom third; bottom margin (roughly lower fifth) blank/stained. Holes and tears at the gutter edge of col. b (upper right near line 5 and at about two-thirds down), with a vellum/paper guard strip along the gutter. Right page: blank modern(?) paper flyleaf/pastedown against brown leather binding; no text.
Visible features in col. a: two words written in a larger, more formal script that look like headings or lemmata, sitting within the column: near line 4 ("[?]uum q(uod) du[?]ones" type, followed by more text on the same line), and about halfway down ("ubium(?) in vo..."), and near the bottom ("nobil[?]...") at right of a line. These may be enlarged lemmata/catchwords set off from the running text; tentative. No rubrics in colour visible; no enlarged initials. Interlinear superscripts abound but they appear to be abbreviation signs, not glosses. Col. b has no such display words visible at overview scale. About 38-40 lines per column.

GENERAL NOTE ON THE HAND: very small, compressed cursive with extreme abbreviation (most words reduced to two-four letters plus superscript letters or suspension strokes). Combined with the staining, most words cannot be resolved with confidence at this resolution. Below I give letter-level readings with tentative expansions in parentheses; "?" follows any uncertain reading. I upscaled crops (2x, Lanczos) of each tile to read; crop paths given per tile. Recurring word read as "tempore"/"tempe" (with "-pe" or "-po" ending and suspension), and a recurring short form "sla"/"sba" preceding it; I cannot settle whether this is "s(ecund)a"/"s(ecund)o", "sola", or "s(ed) a".
